title: External Service Reliability
subtopics: Protecting user experience when external services fail
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of external service reliability and at least two listed subtopics.

content.intro: Learn external service reliability through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: External Service Reliability matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines external service reliability as part of email, background work, and external services. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Retry policies; Timeout budgets; Circuit-breaker concepts; Fallback behavior; Protecting user experience when external services fail. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.text: Protecting user experience when external services fail crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: External Service Reliability
content_blocks.code:
from django.core.mail import send_mail

send_mail("Course update", "A sample message", None, ["learner@example.test"])
content_blocks.expected_output: A configured email backend handles the message according to development/production configuration.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the responsible Django component. Next trace how the example moves through “External Service Reliability” and the related concept “Retry policies”. Predict the result before running or inspecting it. Finally compare the observed behavior with the expected result and the cited official documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Retry policies. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
